about: Hand-kept choices for Map quest (docs/features/map-quest/design.md §3, §4.3). scripts/build-map-quest.py reads this file and refuses an id or verse that does not fit. Ids are OpenBible place ids; disputed candidates are indexes into OpenBible's identifications list for that place.
notesStatus: The disputed-site notes were drafted on 2026-11-07 by the map quest build job from OpenBible's candidate lists, and await the owner's review.

disputed.note: Christian tradition since the fourth century points to Jebel Musa in the south of the Sinai peninsula. Others look to the west or north of the peninsula, to the Negev (Har Karkom) or to north-west Arabia (Jabal al Lawz).
Genesis places Sodom in the Valley of Siddim by the Dead Sea, but not on which shore. Some look south-east of the sea (Bab edh Dhra), others to the plain north of it (Tall el Hammam).
Gomorrah is always named beside Sodom, so the same debate applies: south-east of the Dead Sea (Bab edh Dhra, Numeira) or on the plain north of it.
Most identify it with the spring of Ain el Qudeirat, the largest in the north-east Sinai. Its neighbour Ein Qedeis, which keeps the old name, was proposed first.
The ships of Tarshish sailed far to the west. The long-standing favourite is Tartessos in southern Spain. Others suggest Sardinia, Carthage, or Tarsus in Cilicia.
Solomon's ships brought gold from Ophir, but the Bible never says where it was. Proposals include south-west Arabia, Punt on the African side of the Red Sea, and Sopara on the coast of India.
Luke puts Emmaus sixty stadia, about 11 km, from Jerusalem, and some manuscripts read 160. Candidates include Qalunya and El Qubeibeh nearby, and Emmaus Nicopolis, about 30 km away.
The Church of the Holy Sepulchre has marked the place since the fourth century. Gordon's Calvary, north of the Damascus Gate, was proposed in the nineteenth century.
Two mounds near the north shore of the Sea of Galilee claim it: At Tell, a little inland, and Al Araj, by the water.
Two villages north of Nazareth: Horbat Qana (Khirbet Qana), favoured by many archaeologists, and Kefr Kenna, the traditional site for pilgrims.
Most now place the Philistine city at Tell es Safi. Tell esh Sharia, farther south, was proposed before it.
Zoar lay at the edge of the plain where Lot fled. Most place it at Al Safi, south-east of the Dead Sea. Others put it beside the cities of the plain, wherever those are placed.
Et Tell, east of Bethel, is the classic identification, but its ruins hold no city from Joshua's time, so some propose Khirbet el Maqatir nearby.
